title: The ring of integers is excellent
statement: The commutative ring $\mathbf Z$ is excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring].

source.place: Proposition 15.53.3, Tag 07QW, proposition-ubiquity-excellent, item (3), lines 13385–13412: the integer-ring seed, not just preservation of excellence.

proof.text: The identity extension $\mathbf Q/\mathbf Q$ is purely inseparable by [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] and finite, with basis $1$. Apply [lem-trf-integers-generic-regular-model], obtaining a Noetherian regular ring $B$ and an isomorphism $f:\mathbf Z\to B$. The inverse ideal maps give $f(I)=(b_1,\ldots,b_r)$ iff $I=(f^{-1}(b_1),\ldots,f^{-1}(b_r))$, by applying $f^{-1}$ to sums. Since every ideal of $B$ is finitely generated, so is every ideal of $\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. For a prime $\mathfrak p$, put $\mathfrak q=f(\mathfrak p)$; the isomorphism $\mathbf Z/\mathfrak p\cong B/\mathfrak q$ proves primality. The inverse fraction maps $a/s\mapsto f(a)/f(s)$ and $b/t\mapsto f^{-1}(b)/f^{-1}(t)$ give $\mathbf Z_{\mathfrak p}\cong B_{\mathfrak q}$: denominators avoid corresponding primes and the defining fraction relation is preserved [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. These maps carry the maximal ideals onto one another. Their inverse ideal maps preserve generating lists and prime-chain lengths, hence Noetherianity, dimension and maximal-ideal generator count. Thus each $\mathbf Z_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular local and $\mathbf Z$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: Tag 07QW, proposition-ubiquity-excellent, proof: regular rings are universally catenary; verify regularity of the integer-ring seed.
Tag 07QW, proposition-ubiquity-excellent, proof referring to Tag 07PX, proposition-ubiquity-G-ring, item (3).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-z-localizations-dvr], integer primes are $(0)$ and $(p)$ for rational primes $p$, and $\mathbf Z_{(0)}=\mathbf Q$. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $\kappa((0))=\mathbf Q/(0)$. Let $e:\kappa((0))\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf Q$ send $a+(0)$ to $a$, with inverse $a\mapsto a+(0)$. Given a finite purely inseparable extension $j:\kappa((0))\to L$, put $\iota=j\circ e^{-1}$. The characteristic-zero clause of [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] gives $j(\kappa((0)))=L$, hence $\iota(\mathbf Q)=L$. Injectivity of $\iota$ follows since a nonzero kernel element would give $1=0$. Every $x\in L$ is $\iota(a)\cdot1$ for $a\in\mathbf Q$, so $1$ is a basis; the extension is finite and purely inseparable. Apply [lem-trf-integers-generic-regular-model]. For integers $n$, $\iota(n)=j(n+(0))$, so its image model uses the prescribed residue map. At $(p)$ apply [lem-trf-integers-closed-residue-model] to the given $j:\kappa((p))\to L$. Each image $B\subseteq L$ is a domain: $1\ne0$ in $L$, and $bc=0$ in $B$ forces $b=0$ or $c=0$ in the field $L$. Both models give $B$ finite over $\mathbf Z$ with generator $1$, fractions exhausting $L$, and nonempty open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with every $B_{\mathfrak q}$ regular local. Step 1 supplies Noetherianity; [lem-exc-j2-residue-field-criterion] now gives J-2.

source.place: Tag 07PC, lemma-J-2, implication (4) implies (1), as used in Tag 07PJ, proposition-ubiquity-J-2.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-regular-ring-universally-catenary] to $\mathbf Z$. Step 1 supplies Noetherianity and regularity at every prime, so $\mathbf Z$ is universally catenary.

source.place: Tag 00NM, lemma-CM-ring-catenary, regular-ring consequence; Tag 00NQ, lemma-regular-ring-CM.

proof.text: By [def-exc-excellent-ring], Noetherianity (Step 1), the G-ring condition (Step 2), and J-2 (Step 3) make $\mathbf Z$ quasi-excellent. Universal catenarity (Step 4) then makes it excellent.
